investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource were already at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never wrote any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract violation against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Every new remote-agent pod request is rejected as Unschedulable (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector), so no VM is ever allocated, no agent reaches a ready state, and the eval runner produces an empty evidence object. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs are consuming all available slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, artificially shrinking the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, any single leaked or long-running agent VM would block all probe pods.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup: if cleanup failed on a previous run, orphaned VMs could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots. The runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) but no evidence of successful cleanup is present in the packet.

Lower confidence — node affinity selector targets a node label that no longer matches any node (e.g., after a node pool rotation or label change), reducing the effective schedulable pool to zero even if VM capacity exists elsewhere in the cluster.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource were already at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never wrote any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract violation against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Every new remote-agent pod request is rejected as Unschedulable (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector), so no VM is ever allocated, no agent reaches a ready state, and the eval runner produces an empty evidence object. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150454 — the probe ran for ~150 s, well within the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000 ms, so the failure is driven by the unschedulable pod, not a timeout.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs are consuming all available slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, artificially shrinking the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, any single leaked or long-running agent VM would block all probe pods.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup: if cleanup failed on a previous run, orphaned VMs could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots. The runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) but no evidence of successful cleanup is present in the packet.

Lower confidence — node affinity selector targets a node label that no longer matches any node (e.g., after a node pool rotation or label change), reducing the effective schedulable pool to zero even if VM capacity exists elsewhere in the cluster.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-10T12:37–12:40Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata.peerpods.io/vm workload pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata peerpods resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so zero evidence was collected and all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity: the scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) confirms that the two peerpods-capable nodes are saturated and preemption cannot free capacity. Because the pod never schedules, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) is never reached, the agent VM never starts, and the eval times out after ~150 s returning no evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' and 'No preemption victims found' — pod stuck unscheduled for 146 s before eval timeout.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150559, status=fail, endedAt=2026-08-10T12:40:06.537Z — eval ran to near-timeout without producing any evidence.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message was ever returned, consistent with the probe failing before createAgent() completed.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, confirming the agent was never provisioned.
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=150454, endedAt=2026-08-10T12:35:04 — the creation check failed first with the same unschedulable reason.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=151521, endedAt=2026-08-10T12:37:35 — the state check failed next with the same unschedulable reason.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the step that triggers VM pod scheduling — this step was never reached.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the observed latency of 150559 ms is well below the outage threshold, meaning the failure is a hard scheduling error, not a latency breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two peerpods-capable nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior eval run's leaked VM pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for the new probe pod. Supported by all three sibling checks reporting the same scheduler message.

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration on the probe pod: the 4 non-peerpods nodes are excluded by affinity/selector rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 peerpods nodes. If those rules are overly restrictive or recently changed, capacity that should be available is structurally unavailable.

Tertiary — a prior eval run's remote-agent pod was not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 may not have executed if a previous run was interrupted), leaving a VM slot occupied and reducing available capacity from 2 to 1 or 0.
Lower confidence — the cluster may have scaled down peerpods nodes due to cost or autoscaler policy, reducing the pool from a previously larger size to only 2 nodes.

affectedAreas.reason: degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 (line 187–188); with all 3 checks failing, the feature is at or beyond the outage threshold in the eval system (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189).

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity (kubectl describe nodes) to determine current slot availability and identify which workloads are consuming them.
Check for leaked or stuck pods from prior eval runs that may be holding VM slots; terminate any orphaned remote-agent probe pods to free capacity.
Review the withCleanup() path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm it reliably releases VM resources even when a probe is interrupted or times out, to prevent future slot leakage.

Assess whether the 2-node peerpods pool is sized appropriately for concurrent eval runs plus any production workloads sharing the same VM resource; consider adding peerpods-capable nodes or increasing VM slot limits if the pool is undersized.

Review the pod node affinity and selector rules for remote-agent probe pods to determine whether the 4 non-peerpods nodes are correctly excluded or whether the rules are more restrictive than intended.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false (infra/evals/status/features.json line 185), so this failure does not by itself constitute a required-check outage, but the two required sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) are also failing, which does meet the degradedAfterFailures=1 threshold for the remote-agents feature.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available (allocatable > used) on the peerpods nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different cause (e.g., API-level rejection, auth failure) would need to be investigated.

If the eval probe returned a non-empty evidence object with a different error (e.g., an HTTP 4xx/5xx from the agent API rather than a scheduler message), the root cause would shift from infrastructure capacity to an application-layer failure.
If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the problem would be localized to the runtime probe's pod spec rather than a shared capacity constraint.

If the cluster node count for peerpods-capable nodes is confirmed to be larger than 2 (e.g., autoscaler had not yet scaled up), the capacity exhaustion would be a transient autoscaler lag rather than a hard resource ceiling.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a concurrent workload released VM slots) rather than a persistent capacity problem.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on peerpods nodes before attempting remote agent creation, and emits a warning if available slots fall below a minimum threshold.
Add a resource-leak detection eval that lists all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and alerts if any are in a terminal or stuck state beyond a configurable TTL.

Add a cluster node pool health eval that verifies the expected number of peerpods-capable nodes are Ready and reporting the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, catching autoscaler or node failure scenarios before they exhaust capacity.

Consider a canary eval that runs remote-agent-create with a short timeout specifically to detect scheduling failures early, separate from the full runtime round-trip eval, so scheduling problems are surfaced before the longer runtime probe times out.
